Parasite ecologists say that these critters, too, are finally starting to get the conservation attention they deserveADBy Amber Dance9:00 AM CST on November 18, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleGiardia lamblia parasite as Closup – 3D Rendering. This story was originally published by Knowable Magazine.Powered By 10 ShareNextStayIn the 1980s, biologists rounded up every last California condor for captive breeding. It was an unprecedented conservation project with stunning success: Today, the birds number more than 600.But for some ecologists, there’s a distressing corollary: The birds were reportedly treated with pesticides that killed condor parasites, including one unique to these birds, the condor louse Colpocephalum californici. The condor louse became a poster child for parasite extinction.Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
